faq.item.1.a: Hold Corretora is a solutions ecosystem focused on protection, planning, and wealth structuring for individuals and businesses, operating independently with an integrated vision.
faq.item.2.q: What makes Hold different from a traditional brokerage?
faq.item.2.a: Our work goes beyond intermediation. We combine analytical insight, market understanding, and broad sector access to support more efficient and sustainable decisions.
faq.item.3.a: Yes. We work with freedom of analysis and broad curation, prioritizing what truly makes sense for each client.
faq.item.4.q: Which institutions does Hold work with?
faq.item.4.a: Hold has access to more than 60 strategic partners, including insurers, health operators, and consortium administrators, expanding possibilities and enabling a more complete, competitive offering aligned with each client's needs.
faq.item.5.q: How does Hold ensure security and credibility?
faq.item.5.a: We work exclusively with nationally regulated and recognized institutions, maintaining transparency, close monitoring, and accountability in every operation.
faq.item.6.q: Does Hold only serve end clients?
faq.item.6.a: No. We also develop commercial alliances with companies, professionals, and firms looking to expand their reach through a solid and specialized operation.
faq.item.7.q: How does Hold's operating model work?
faq.item.7.a: Before any recommendation, we seek to understand objectives, context, and priorities to structure alternatives that are coherent with each reality.
faq.item.8.q: Does Hold serve both individuals and businesses?
faq.item.8.a: Yes. Our operation is prepared for both personal and family demands as well as corporate and wealth management needs.
faq.item.9.a: We have specialists across different areas, enabling an integrated, technical approach aligned with the needs of each client profile.
faq.item.10.q: Why do companies and partners choose Hold?
faq.item.10.a: For the combination of close relationships, analytical capability, operational agility, and broad access to the sector's leading institutions.
faq.item.11.q: Does Hold's work go beyond sales?
faq.item.11.a: Yes. We take part in building more conscious decisions, accompanying clients and partners closely and continuously.
faq.item.12.q: How does Hold keep up with sector developments?
faq.item.12.a: We maintain constant learning, proximity to relevant institutions, and continuous monitoring of economic and regulatory movements.
faq.item.13.a: To build lasting relationships grounded in trust, clarity, responsibility, and value creation.
faq.item.14.q: What makes Hold a long-term partner?
faq.item.14.a: The combination of technical knowledge, integrated vision, close relationships, and the ability to adapt to the needs of each scenario.
faq.item.15.q: What is Hold's strength in the sector?
faq.item.15.a: We operate with broad access to the country's leading institutions, a multi-sector approach, and the ability to serve everything from individual demands to complex corporate structures, always with strategic vision and commercial independence.

saudeV2.faq.title: Frequently asked questions about health plans
saudeV2.faq.q1.q: What's the difference between individual, group-by-affiliation and corporate plans?
saudeV2.faq.q1.b1: Health plans vary according to the contracting model and the beneficiary's eligibility.
saudeV2.faq.q1.b3: Contracted directly by an individual, with coverage for the holder and their dependents.
saudeV2.faq.q1.b5: Aimed at professionals affiliated with eligible class entities, unions, associations or professional councils.
saudeV2.faq.q1.b7: Aimed at companies of different sizes — including MEIs, SMBs and large operations — through a contract tied to the company's CNPJ.
saudeV2.faq.q1.b8: Each model has specific characteristics related to:
saudeV2.faq.q1.b9: eligibility|price adjustments|contract rules|group composition|waiting periods|contracting formats
saudeV2.faq.q1.b10: That's why a proper analysis of profile and need is essential before contracting.
saudeV2.faq.q2.q: Can a MEI (sole proprietor) contract a corporate plan?
saudeV2.faq.q2.b1: Yes. The Individual Micro-Entrepreneur (MEI) can contract a corporate health plan, as long as they meet the criteria set by the operator and hold an active CNPJ within the regulatory requirements.
saudeV2.faq.q2.b3: time since company opening|minimum number of lives|operator|sales region|contracted model
saudeV2.faq.q2.b4: In many cases, the corporate plan can be a strategically cost-effective alternative for formalized professionals and their families.

saudeV2.faq.q4.q: How do I choose the right plan?
saudeV2.faq.q4.b1: Choosing a health plan involves more than comparing prices. It's important to analyze factors such as:
saudeV2.faq.q4.b2: usage profile|age range|hospital network|geographic coverage|accommodation|co-payment|financial predictability|family or business needs|medium- and long-term horizon
saudeV2.faq.q4.b3: Different models can also offer specific advantages depending on the client's profile.
saudeV2.faq.q4.b4: HOLD performs a consultative, personalized analysis to help build the solution best suited to each reality.
saudeV2.faq.q5.q: What is a waiting period in a health plan?
saudeV2.faq.q5.b1: A waiting period is the time, counted from the start of contract validity, during which certain types of coverage cannot yet be fully used.
saudeV2.faq.q5.b2: Brazilian Law nº 9.656/98 sets maximum waiting periods for regulated plans, including:
saudeV2.faq.q5.b3: 24 hours for urgent and emergency care|up to 180 days for consultations, exams, hospitalizations and other procedures|300 days for full-term delivery|up to 24 months for temporary partial coverage related to pre-existing diseases or injuries
saudeV2.faq.q6.q: Is it possible to reduce or carry over waiting periods?
saudeV2.faq.q6.b1: Yes, in some cases. Depending on the beneficiary's history and the operator's rules, there may be:
saudeV2.faq.q6.b2: waiting-period reduction|carry-over of periods already served|portability of waiting periods|specific promotional campaigns
saudeV2.faq.q6.b3: The analysis depends on factors such as:
saudeV2.faq.q6.b4: time spent on the previous plan|compatibility between products|documentation provided|ANS regulatory rules|operator criteria
saudeV2.faq.q6.b5: Each situation should be evaluated individually.
saudeV2.faq.q7.q: Do health plans follow ANS regulation and Law nº 9.656/98?
saudeV2.faq.q7.b1: Yes. Regulated health plans follow the guidelines established by the National Supplementary Health Agency (ANS) and by Law nº 9.656/98, the main supplementary health legislation in Brazil.
saudeV2.faq.q7.b2: The regulation sets rules related to:
saudeV2.faq.q7.b3: mandatory minimum coverage|waiting periods|urgent and emergency care|price adjustments|portability|pre-existing diseases and injuries|beneficiary rights|operator responsibilities|care segmentation|contract operation
saudeV2.faq.q7.b4: In addition, ANS also defines the List of Health Procedures and Events, which represents the mandatory minimum coverage of regulated plans.
saudeV2.faq.q7.b5: HOLD helps clients understand these rules to provide more clarity, security and predictability when making decisions.
saudeV2.faq.q8.q: How do urgent and emergency care services work in health plans?
saudeV2.faq.q8.b1: Urgent and emergency care follows specific rules defined by Law nº 9.656/98 and ANS regulation.
saudeV2.faq.q8.b3: Situations involving immediate risk to life or the possibility of irreparable injury to the patient, as declared by a physician.
saudeV2.faq.q8.b8: In regulated plans, the maximum waiting period for urgent and emergency care is 24 hours after the start of contract validity.
saudeV2.faq.q8.b9: After this period, the beneficiary becomes entitled to coverage according to the contracted plan's segmentation and contractual rules.
saudeV2.faq.q8.b10: How does coverage work in hospital plans?
saudeV2.faq.q8.b11: In plans with hospital coverage, urgent and emergency care may include:
saudeV2.faq.q8.b12: emergency room|exams|procedures|medications used during care|hospitalizations|surgeries|treatments needed to stabilize the clinical condition
saudeV2.faq.q8.b13: How does it work in exclusively outpatient plans?
saudeV2.faq.q8.b14: In exclusively outpatient plans, urgent and emergency coverage is limited to the first 12 hours of care.
saudeV2.faq.q8.b15: If hospitalization is needed after that period, specific rules set in the contract and in ANS regulation may apply. In such cases, there may be:
saudeV2.faq.q8.b16: patient transfer|referral to the public health system (SUS)|continuity of care according to the contracted segmentation
saudeV2.faq.q8.b17: What happens in cases of pre-existing disease or injury?
saudeV2.faq.q8.b18: When there is Temporary Partial Coverage (CPT) related to a declared pre-existing disease or injury, there may be temporary limitations for:
saudeV2.faq.q8.b19: high-complexity procedures|surgeries|high-tech beds related to the declared condition
saudeV2.faq.q8.b20: Even so, the care needed to stabilize an urgent or emergency condition remains guaranteed as set out in the legislation.
saudeV2.faq.q8.b21: Why is it important to review the contract?
saudeV2.faq.q8.b22: Coverage conditions may vary according to:
saudeV2.faq.q8.b23: plan model|care segmentation|coverage area|accommodation type|co-payment|waiting periods|CPT|operator rules
saudeV2.faq.q8.b24: HOLD helps clients understand these conditions, seeking more clarity, security and predictability when choosing the most suitable plan.
